chunks: ʿAlī narrated from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who seizes a thief: should he bring him forward or leave him?

He said: “Indeed, Ṣafwān ibn Umayyah was lying down in al-Masjid al-Ḥarām. He placed his cloak down and went out to pour out water. When he returned, he found that his cloak had been stolen. He said: ‘Who took my cloak?’ So he went seeking it, then seized the one who had it and brought him to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: ‘Cut off his hand.’ Ṣafwān said: ‘Would his hand be cut off because of my cloak, O Messenger of Allah?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Then I give it to him as a gift.’ The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: ‘Why did this not happen before you brought him to me?’”
I said: “So the Imam holds the same position, when the matter is brought to him?” He said: “Yes.”
He said: And I asked him about pardoning before the matter reaches the Imam, and he said: “It is good.”

key_terms.اِقْطَعُوا يَدَهُ: the order to carry out the hadd punishment for qualifying theft
key_terms.رِدَاءَهُ: his cloak, the stolen property in this case
key_terms.فَرَفَعَهُ: he brought him forward to the authority for judgment
key_terms.ٱللِّصَّ: the thief who committed the theft
key_terms.ٱلنَّبِيِّ صَلَّى ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِ: the Prophet as the judicial authority in the report
key_terms.ٱلْإِمَامِ: the Imam, who holds equivalent judicial authority here
key_terms.ٱلْعَفْوِ: pardon or remission by the victim before formal referral

ai.seo_question: Can a theft victim forgive the thief before or after the case is brought to the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that in the case of theft, pardoning or waiving one’s claim is acceptable before the case is formally brought to the Imam. Once the matter is raised to the Imam or legitimate authority, the legal process proceeds and private waiver is no longer effective. The narration supports the judicial authority of the Imam in implementing prescribed punishments.
